mortgage.answer: A mortgage payment estimate separates loan principal and interest from taxes, insurance and other ownership costs. Use the initial total for starting cash flow and the schedule for later changes.

results.label: Monthly principal & interest
results.meaning: The scheduled loan payment before taxes, insurance and entered ownership costs.

results.label: Initial monthly total
results.meaning: The first modeled payment including initial ownership costs and applicable extra principal; later costs may grow.

results.label: Total interest
results.meaning: Interest paid over the modeled loan, excluding property taxes and insurance.

compare: Hold home price and loan term fixed; change only the down payment to compare financing needs.
Then compare interest rates while leaving taxes, insurance and fees unchanged.
checks: Enter annual taxes and insurance with the matching dollar or percentage unit.
Do not compare a principal-and-interest payment with another quote that includes escrow.
Paying off a mortgage does not remove property taxes, insurance or maintenance.
For requested 80% PMI cancellation, use the appraisal at purchase if below the purchase price; a current market appraisal is not the original value.

Automatic PMI uses an assumed credit score range (default 740–759) and a dated base-rate card. Select Manual to use an actual lender quote; PMI is already included in the initial monthly total and schedule costs.

mortgage-payoff.answer: Extra mortgage principal can shorten repayment and reduce future loan interest. Compare strategies using the same current balance, regular payment and interest rate.

results.label: Current principal balance
results.meaning: The balance at the start of this projection, not the original home price.

results.label: Interest saved
results.meaning: Baseline future interest minus strategy future interest under the same modeled loan assumptions.

results.label: Years to payoff
results.meaning: Actual modeled payment count divided by the payment frequency; the last payment is capped at what remains.

compare: Run the normal monthly strategy first, then enter one extra monthly amount.
Test a lump sum separately before combining it with recurring extras; keep the start dates consistent.
checks: Use a lender statement for your current balance and regular principal-and-interest payment.
A half payment every two weeks produces 26 payments per year; twice a month produces 24.
Lender payoff fees, penalties and daily interest since the last payment are outside this model.

rent.answer: This rent affordability calculator uses the lower of your selected rent-to-income limit and the room left under your total-debt limit. The result is a planning ceiling based on gross income.

results.label: Gross monthly income
results.meaning: Income normalized to a month using the selected pay frequency; this is not after-tax take-home pay.

results.label: Monthly rent budget
results.meaning: The smaller ratio-based allowance after accounting for entered monthly debt, floored at zero.

compare: Keep income fixed and compare the budget before and after a change in debt payments.
Try a lower rent-to-income ratio, then check the remaining cash against actual take-home pay and living expenses.
checks: Choose the frequency of the entered income instead of converting it twice.
Utilities, food, deposits, moving costs and other expenses are not automatically deducted.
The selected ratios are assumptions and do not establish landlord approval.

house-affordability.answer: An affordability estimate converts an entered housing budget into a home price after down payment, loan interest and ownership costs. It is not a mortgage approval or an appraisal.

results.label: Monthly housing budget
results.meaning: The spending ceiling under the entered housing and total-debt ratios, or the budget you supply.

results.label: Estimated home price
results.meaning: The price that fits the modeled loan payment and selected ownership costs.

results.label: Down payment
results.meaning: Cash applied to the purchase price; closing costs may require additional cash.

compare: Compare two interest rates while keeping income, debts, down payment and ownership costs unchanged.
Then test the effect of taxes and insurance separately, rather than changing every input at once.
checks: Verify whether down payment and annual ownership costs are dollars or percentages.
An insurance cost must be entered if needed; mortgage insurance is not automatically underwritten.
Qualification also depends on lender rules and information outside this budget model.

auto-loan.answer: A car payment estimate depends on the amount financed, interest rate, loan length, trade-in, rebates and entered taxes and fees. Compare total cost as well as monthly payment.

results.label: Sales tax
results.meaning: Tax calculated from the entered rate and selected purchase-tax treatment; special local rules may be missing.

results.label: Payment per period
results.meaning: The modeled installment on the financed balance; a longer term can lower it without lowering total interest.

results.label: Total payments
results.meaning: Loan installments over the schedule; it is not a complete ownership-cost total including fuel, maintenance and insurance.

compare: Use the same vehicle price, trade-in, down payment and taxes for both financing offers.
Change the rate or term independently, then compare total interest and required upfront cash.
checks: Outstanding trade-in debt is separate from the trade-in value.
Check whether taxes and fees are financed or paid upfront.
A payment quote that includes optional warranties is not directly comparable unless those costs are entered.

savings.answer: Savings growth depends on starting money, deposit timing, the rate convention and compounding. The inflation-adjusted result expresses purchasing power rather than an additional account balance.

results.label: Ending balance
results.meaning: The modeled nominal balance after contributions, growth and modeled interest tax.

results.label: Total contributions
results.meaning: Starting money plus later deposits; it does not mean interest earned.

results.label: Inflation-adjusted balance
results.meaning: Ending balance divided by accumulated assumed inflation over the saving period.

compare: Compare two deposit amounts with the same return, compounding and timing.
Then change the return assumption separately; check how inflation changes purchasing power without changing the nominal account balance.
checks: Select APY for an effective annual yield; compounding is ignored in that setting. Select Nominal interest rate for a stated rate plus compounding frequency.
Beginning-of-period deposits earn interest sooner than end-of-period deposits.
No bank offers or current high-yield account rates are fetched.

retirement.answer: Retirement planning separates the target fund, future saving and retirement withdrawals. Select the mode that answers your question and read its return, inflation and payment-timing assumptions.

results.label: Required savings at retirement
results.meaning: The target balance for the modeled inflation-adjusted retirement income gap.

results.label: Projected surplus / shortfall
results.meaning: Projected retirement savings minus the target; a negative amount is a modeled funding shortfall.

results.label: Initial monthly withdrawal
results.meaning: The first retirement-month payment in Monthly Withdrawal; subsequent payments grow with the entered inflation assumption.

compare: Compare lifespans with the same balance and return to see how a longer withdrawal period changes income.
Test a lower return separately, leaving contributions and inflation unchanged, before changing the saving plan.
checks: Do not add a monthly contribution and an annual contribution if they describe the same deposits.
In Required Savings, other retirement income is entered as a monthly retirement amount and modeled as inflation-indexed.
Savings Longevity uses fixed withdrawals; Monthly Withdrawal models inflation increases. These are different scenarios.

heloc.answer: This HELOC model assumes the full balance is outstanding at the start, interest-only payments during draw and amortizing payments afterward. The rate is held fixed throughout the projection.

results.label: Monthly draw payment
results.meaning: Interest plus the annual account fee allocated over draw months for an average monthly cost.

results.label: Monthly repayment
results.meaning: The amortizing payment after draw; the modeled draw-period annual fee stops at this transition.

results.label: Net initial proceeds after closing costs
results.meaning: Loan balance minus entered closing costs; financing fees on top of principal is not modeled.

compare: Hold balance and terms fixed; compare a no-fee case with the entered closing cost and annual account fee.
Then change the interest rate separately to see the payment effect; this does not forecast future variable-rate resets.
checks: The draw period does not simulate gradual new advances or changing balances.
An allocated monthly account fee is not a prediction of the lender’s actual annual billing date.
Fees can change estimated APR even when the contract interest rate stays the same.

401k.answer: The 401(k) projection grows the opening balance once per year, then adds employee and employer contributions at year end. A separate retirement schedule illustrates before-tax withdrawals.

results.label: Employee contributions
results.meaning: New employee deposits during the projection; the starting balance is shown separately.

results.label: Projected 401(k) balance
results.meaning: Starting savings plus modeled contributions and investment growth at retirement.

results.label: Initial monthly retirement withdrawal
results.meaning: The illustrated first withdrawal using life expectancy and inflation; it does not enforce RMD rules.

compare: Change the employee contribution rate while keeping salary, retirement age and return unchanged.
Use Maximize Employer Match to examine matching tiers before comparing higher contribution rates.
checks: Future years hold the stated 2026 limits fixed rather than predicting future limit increases.
Match limits describe eligible salary bands and are not the same as the employer match percentage.
The retirement income illustration assumes full vesting and excludes taxes and fees.

debt-payoff.answer: Debt payoff plans pay each minimum first, then allocate extra money by your selected strategy. Avalanche prioritizes high APR; snowball prioritizes small remaining balances.

results.label: Months until debt-free
results.meaning: The number of modeled monthly payments needed to clear all listed debts.

results.label: Total interest
results.meaning: Interest accrued across all debts under the selected strategy and budget.

results.label: Total paid
results.meaning: Starting balances plus modeled interest; new borrowing and additional fees are excluded.

compare: Hold balances, APRs, minimums, extra payments and rollover choice constant; change only Debt Avalanche versus Debt Snowball.
Load the worked examples below: the same $6,000 debts and initial $300 monthly budget show both strategies and both rollover choices.
Compare interest and months first. Changing rollover changes the later budget, so review it separately from the strategy.
checks: APR values in the debt list are annual percentages; balances and minimum payments are dollar amounts.
Keeping the total payment fixed rolls freed payments into other debts; turning rollover off changes the budget.
Snowball does not guarantee the lowest interest bill.

rmd.answer: This owner-account RMD estimate divides the prior year-end balance by the applicable life-expectancy divisor. Verify the account type, distribution year and selected table before using the amount.

results.label: Age in distribution year
results.meaning: Age reached during the selected distribution year, calculated from the entered birth year.

results.label: Distribution period
results.meaning: The divisor from the modeled IRS table, not the number of years the account is guaranteed to last.

results.label: Annual RMD
results.meaning: The calculated annual distribution requirement under the selected table and entered account balance.

compare: Use the same account balance to compare the applicable divisors for adjacent distribution years.
Keep the distribution year fixed when checking whether the spouse-related table selection changes the divisor.
checks: Use the required prior December 31 balance rather than substituting today’s balance.
Inherited accounts and some still-working exceptions are outside this owner-account model.
A displayed annual RMD does not determine its income-tax treatment or payment deadline.

take-home-paycheck.answer: Take-home pay here is estimated from gross pay, entered deductions and an allocation of annual federal tax. It is not a full payroll-withholding calculation and may differ from an employer paycheck.

results.label: Gross pay per period
results.meaning: Pay from this job converted to the selected pay frequency before modeled deductions.

results.label: Annual federal tax allocated to this job
results.meaning: Household federal tax with this job minus the other-job baseline under the annual allocation model.

results.label: Take-home pay per period
results.meaning: This job’s modeled pay after deductions and allocated taxes; other-job income is not added to this paycheck.

compare: Compare two contribution amounts with the same job income, filing status and pay frequency.
Compare annual totals before comparing pay periods; weekly, biweekly and semimonthly schedules have different counts.
checks: Do not enter the same income as both this job’s pay and other-job income.
State and local rates are entered estimates, not complete jurisdiction-specific returns.
W-4 elections, year-to-date payroll and IRS Publication 15-T withholding are not fully modeled.

pmi.answer: Conventional PMI pricing and cancellation are separate questions. Original loan-to-value determines the illustrative premium; the original-value 80% request, original-schedule 78% automatic termination and month-after-midpoint rule determine distinct potential ending dates.

results.label: Initial monthly PMI
results.meaning: The modeled initial conventional premium, excluding home insurance and property taxes.

results.label: 80% request benchmark
results.meaning: An opportunity to apply after the qualifying payment; approval and conditions still apply.

results.label: Scheduled 78% benchmark
results.meaning: The original-schedule automatic threshold if payments are current, separate from actual accelerated LTV.

compare: Hold price, appraisal and loan terms fixed; compare an illustrative rate with your lender’s annual quote.
Then compare extra principal and the requested versus automatic scenarios without changing original value.
checks: Use original value, not a new appreciated appraisal, for HPA thresholds.
Current payments are required for automatic termination.
Do not add the two alternative PMI schedule columns together.

biweekly-mortgage.answer: Paying half a monthly payment every two weeks produces 26 half-payments, equal to 13 monthly payments per modeled year. The calculator compares this with ordinary monthly payments and with a monthly plan that has the same annual outlay.

results.label: Biweekly payment
results.meaning: Half the normal monthly P&I plus entered extra per biweekly payment.

results.label: Extra annual outlay versus monthly
results.meaning: Additional annual cash required by the 26-payment plan.

results.label: Matched-budget monthly total interest
results.meaning: A monthly alternative with the same annual payment budget.

compare: Compare standard monthly with 26 credited payments per year.
Compare biweekly with the equal-annual-budget monthly alternative to separate timing from extra principal.
checks: 26 biweekly payments differ from 24 semimonthly payments.
Verify how a servicer credits partial payments and whether fees apply.
The model uses annual rate divided by 26, not daily calendar accrual.

discount-points.answer: Compare two fixed-rate loan quotes with the same principal and term. Points cost 1% of principal per point, but the rate reduction must come from the lender’s actual quote. The comparison distinguishes monthly cash savings from interest-and-fee savings at a sale or refinancing horizon.

results.label: Net borrowing-cost savings at horizon (B vs A)
results.meaning: Interest and upfront costs saved by offer B; positive favors B, negative favors A.

results.label: Net cash-flow savings at horizon
results.meaning: Payment savings less additional upfront cost, excluding the balance difference.

results.label: First net-cost break-even month
results.meaning: The first modeled month that B’s interest/fee cost is no higher than A’s, not a guarantee of permanent advantage.

compare: Enter two actual same-principal, same-term Loan Estimate rate/point quotes.
Change only the sale/refinance holding period to compare short- and long-term costs.
checks: One point is a fee equal to 1% of principal, not a fixed rate reduction.
Points and fees are paid in cash in this model.
Compare cash-flow savings and remaining principal together.

coast-fire.answer: Find the retirement portfolio needed today to grow toward a future spending target without further deposits. Below that threshold, this model adds monthly investments until the first whole-month crossing, then stops deposits. It does not fund living costs before retirement.

results.label: Coast FIRE number today
results.meaning: The invested balance required now under your budget, withdrawal rate, return, inflation and retirement-age assumptions. It is not the full retirement portfolio target.

results.label: Age at Coast FIRE
results.meaning: The first modeled month when the portfolio meets the moving Coast threshold. “Not reached by target age” means the model found no crossing within your selected horizon.

results.label: Current gap to Coast threshold
results.meaning: Today’s threshold minus the current retirement portfolio, floored at zero. Monthly deposits can close the moving gap; this is not an extra immediate-payment requirement.

results.label: Retirement balance on modeled path
results.meaning: The projected balance after deposits stop at the first crossing, or after deposits continue to retirement if the threshold is never reached. Amounts retain today’s purchasing power.

compare: Calculate your starting plan and read both the current threshold and expected crossing time.
Open calculation details to compare return and target retirement-age thresholds while keeping other inputs fixed.
To compare the full timeline, change one input in the form, calculate again and compare the resulting age and path. Use the existing CSV or result-summary exports to retain each scenario.
checks: Every dollar amount is in today’s USD. Do not inflate the retirement budget a second time.
The return field is nominal, after fees. Inflation is deducted through the exact real-growth relationship.
Monthly deposits maintain purchasing power and end at the first modeled crossing. No pre-retirement withdrawals are modeled.
Default rates are illustrations. Lower returns, higher spending or different withdrawal assumptions can change the conclusion; no probability of success is calculated.

noi.answer: NOI separates a property’s operations from financing. Choose one reporting period for every income and expense field, then review the annual reconciliation before interpreting cash flow or returns.

results.label: Annual net operating income
results.meaning: Effective annual operating income minus annual operating expenses, before debt service, capital costs and owner income tax.

results.label: Monthly net operating income
results.meaning: Annual NOI divided by 12, not a month-by-month seasonal forecast.

results.label: NOI margin
results.meaning: NOI divided by effective operating income. Undefined at zero effective income.

compare: Calculate with scheduled rent before vacancy. Review each annualized income and cost row.
Change one operating assumption, such as vacancy or repairs, while holding other entries fixed.
Compare the NOI difference before considering a separate financing or value model.
checks: All monetary fields use the selected reporting period. The selector does not convert typed values.
Management is an entered dollar cost, not an automatically applied percentage.
Do not count mortgage payments, capital improvements or replacement reserves as operating expenses in this model.

fire.answer: This is a full FIRE savings target, not the smaller present-value Coast milestone. The projection ends when assets first reach the target, or at your selected age limit.

results.label: FIRE portfolio target
results.meaning: Annual portfolio-funded spending divided by the entered withdrawal rate, in today’s USD.

results.label: Age at modeled FIRE target
results.meaning: First whole-month crossing under constant returns and monthly deposits. No age is inferred if the target is not reached within the limit.

results.label: Portfolio at projection endpoint
results.meaning: Savings at the crossing or age limit. This is not a projected balance after retirement withdrawals.

compare: Calculate a budget and investment plan using consistent real-dollar inputs.
Change monthly investing or the budget separately and compare the first crossing.
Use Coast FIRE only for the distinct question of growing to a later retirement target without further deposits.
checks: All money is in today’s purchasing power. Nominal return and inflation are separate inputs.
Monthly deposits maintain purchasing power and stop when the savings projection ends.
Reaching a withdrawal-rate sizing target does not establish withdrawal safety or access to retirement accounts.

mirr.answer: MIRR transforms payments and receipts using different rate assumptions. Reconcile time-zero outflow cost with terminal reinvested receipts before comparing periodic and annual rates.

results.label: Effective annual MIRR
results.meaning: Compound annual equivalent of the calculated periodic MIRR, not a forecast or actual annual profit.

results.label: MIRR per cash-flow period
results.meaning: Equivalent rate for the selected yearly, quarterly or monthly interval.

results.label: Present value of outflows
results.meaning: Positive magnitude of all negative payments discounted to time zero at the financing assumption.

compare: Enter the full signed series from time zero, preserving each zero interval.
Hold the series fixed and change only financing or reinvestment assumptions.
For a spacing change, remember that both rate inputs stay effective annual rates while the horizon and equivalent period rates change.
checks: One number per line; no labels or thousands separators.
Both positive and negative cash flows are required. Internal blank lines are rejected.
Nonannual comparisons with Excel must use equivalent period rates; dated XIRR is a different model.

rental-property.answer: Read property operations, financing cash flow and sale proceeds separately. First-year cap rate and cash-on-cash are not the full holding-period annual IRR.

results.label: First-year cash flow
results.meaning: First-year operating income less operating costs and modeled mortgage payments; excludes the terminal sale.

results.label: Capitalization rate
results.meaning: First-year NOI divided by entered after-repair value, or purchase price if that value is zero.

results.label: First-year cash-on-cash
results.meaning: First-year cash flow divided by initial cash including closing costs and initial repairs.

results.label: Total investment profit
results.meaning: Sum of yearly operating cash flows and net sale proceeds, minus initial cash. It is not an annual percentage.

compare: Review the year table and initial cash before comparing return percentages.
Hold operations fixed and change only financing or the known sale price.
Read yearly cash flow and full project profit together; a positive year does not guarantee a profitable sale.
checks: Monthly rent and other income become annual amounts; recurring expenses are annual inputs.
Vacancy applies to rent only; management applies to effective rent plus other income.
No tax depreciation, income tax, capital-gains tax, appraisal or market forecast is generated.

debt-consolidation.answer: Compare future interest plus the origination fee against the current avalanche payoff benchmark. A lower monthly payment alone does not show a saving.

results.label: Payment per period
results.meaning: The new fixed monthly principal-and-interest payment, including a financed fee in principal when selected.

results.label: Current plan total interest
results.meaning: Future interest from a fixed combined monthly budget equal to entered minimums, with avalanche rollover.

results.label: Interest and fee savings
results.meaning: Current-plan interest minus new-loan interest minus the origination fee. Negative means the new scenario has higher modeled borrowing costs.

compare: Keep existing debt balances, payments and rates fixed.
Compare the offered rate, term and fee, checking whether the fee is financed.
Review payment affordability and total cost separately; different terms are not equal monthly-budget comparisons.
checks: Debt amounts have no thousands separators; every line has name, balance, payment and APR.
Current minimum amounts are fixed entries, not declining issuer formulas.
No new borrowing, credit-score prediction, approval or government consolidation benefit is inferred.

business-loan.answer: Separate base loan amount, repayment balance, net cash proceeds and payment including insurance. The cash-flow APR reflects entered fees, not loan eligibility.

results.label: Payment including insurance
results.meaning: Periodic loan installment plus the entered insurance charge per payment.

results.label: Net proceeds after fees
results.meaning: Net initial cash in the model. Financed fees increase principal; upfront or deducted fees lower net initial cash on a common comparison basis.

results.label: Nominal APR including insurance
results.meaning: Periodic cash-flow rate multiplied by payments per year. Not an automatically supplied lender quote or an effective annual yield.

compare: Enter a consistent base amount, term, rate and repayment frequency.
Change the fee treatment while holding the offered base loan fixed.
Compare net initial cash, installments and total cost rather than payment alone.
checks: Compounding and payment frequency are separate choices.
Loan Total payments and its table exclude separate insurance; include those charges when reconciling combined cash outflow.
No automatic SBA program rules, variable-rate resets, factor-rate pricing or approval calculation.

budget.answer: Normalize income, spending, debt and savings allocations to a monthly equivalent, then check the unallocated balance after the entered flat-tax assumption.

results.label: Monthly take-home income
results.meaning: All entered income normalized to monthly, less the single assumed tax percentage. This is not a payroll-tax computation.

results.label: Monthly spending and saving
results.meaning: Monthly equivalents of all non-income categories, including the named saving allocations.

results.label: Monthly surplus / deficit
results.meaning: Take-home income less spending and saving allocations. A positive result is still unallocated; a negative result is a shortfall.

compare: Set the correct frequency for every income and outflow line.
Review the flat tax rate, especially if entries are already take-home amounts.
Change one spending or savings allocation and compare the resulting surplus.
checks: Biweekly uses 26 occurrences per year and Weekly uses 52, divided by 12.
Saving is already included in the outflow total; do not deduct it again.
No automatic needs/wants classification, tax return or bank data connection.

break-even.answer: Choose quantity, target profit or required price. Whole-unit quantity results round upward; price mode retains internal fractional-cent precision.

results.label: Break-even units (whole units)
results.meaning: The smallest whole unit count covering fixed costs at the entered positive unit contribution.

results.label: Revenue at whole units
results.meaning: Selling price multiplied by rounded-up units; it can differ from theoretical continuous break-even sales.

results.label: Contribution margin per unit
results.meaning: Price minus variable unit cost, before covering fixed cost.

results.label: Required selling price
results.meaning: In Price mode, variable unit cost plus fixed cost and target profit divided by entered volume.

compare: Keep the product and fixed-cost period consistent.
Change price or unit variable cost separately when comparing quantity.
Compare theoretical and whole-unit quantities, or use Price mode for a specified volume.
checks: Quantity modes require selling price above variable unit cost.
Single-product model: no weighted multi-product mix or variable capacity step costs.
Social Security, mortgage-point and advertising break-even are different models.

roi.answer: Return on investment (ROI) is gain or loss divided by initial cost. Total ROI covers the entire holding period; annualized ROI is its compound yearly equivalent. Enter the full amount returned, including the principal recovered, rather than the gain alone. This calculator uses an initial commitment and a terminal returned value; dated intermediate cash flows need a different model.

results.label: Investment gain
results.meaning: Terminal returned amount minus initial cost; returned amount means full terminal value, not gain alone.

results.label: Return on investment
results.meaning: Total gain divided by cost, independent of holding length.

results.label: Annualized return
results.meaning: Compound annual equivalent using entered years or actual elapsed days divided by 365 in Dates mode.

compare: Define cost and returned amount consistently, including relevant charges once.
Compare total ROI with annualized return at the same duration.
Use Rental Property, Investment, or Dated Cash Flows when operating income or additional deposits have their own timing.
checks: Cost must be positive and duration greater than zero. Negative returns are supported.
Dates mode uses actual days / 365; a leap-year interval can differ from one entered year.
No automatic taxes, advertising attribution, valuation or universal good-return threshold.

investment.answer: Choose the missing variable, then compare ending balance, contributions and earnings on a consistent rate and timing basis.

results.label: Ending balance
results.meaning: Projected nominal balance after contributions and the entered simplified tax assumption.

results.label: Total contributions
results.meaning: Starting balance plus deposits; investment earnings are separate.

results.label: Return Rate
results.meaning: In that solve mode, an implied nominal annual rate with the selected compounding. Not an available investment quote.

results.label: Invest Length
results.meaning: First whole month reaching the goal, shown in years.

compare: Hold the starting balance and horizon fixed when comparing deposit amounts.
Compare beginning and end timing separately from rates.
Review inflation-adjusted value separately from nominal balance.
checks: Compounding frequency applies to a nominal annual rate.
Tax is a simplified rate on positive interest at year-end or the final partial year; no loss carryforward.
No actual market returns, account tax rules or withdrawal sequence simulation.

irr.answer: Read each detected rate with the exact signed cash-flow times. Multiple roots are an ambiguity to inspect, not a choice of which return to advertise.

results.label: Annual IRR 1
results.meaning: A detected effective annual rate that makes modeled NPV zero; the first root is not a preferred recommendation.

compare: Keep zero periods so later flows do not move earlier.
Match timing and frequency before comparing with a spreadsheet.
Use Dated Cash Flows for actual calendar dates and MIRR for explicit reinvestment assumptions.
checks: Enter initial investment as a positive amount; the tool converts it to an outflow.
Monthly flows still produce effective annual headline rates.
The bounded search does not guarantee every root; IRR is not a risk measure.

annuity.answer: Separate the accumulation balance from the money contributed. A projected future balance is not a lifetime payout quote.

results.label: Annuity future value
results.meaning: Starting principal and deposits grown at the entered constant effective annual return.

results.label: Total additions
results.meaning: Monthly and annual additions after the initial principal.

results.label: Growth
results.meaning: Future value minus all contributions, without contract fees or tax calculations.

compare: Hold return and total contribution amounts fixed to compare timing.
Use Annuity Payout only after defining a balance to withdraw.
Compare a lower return assumption before interpreting a long horizon.
checks: Annual return is effective; monthly growth uses its equivalent rate.
First-row addition includes the starting principal.
No insurance guarantees, riders, surrender charges or tax treatment are priced.

annuity-payout.answer: Review how much is principal returned, how much is modeled earnings and when the last payout occurs. The payout frequency and final payment date matter when comparing scenarios.

results.label: Payment each period
results.meaning: Fix Length’s regular payout for the selected frequency; a partial final period can produce a different last amount.

results.label: Payout duration in years
results.meaning: Fix Payment’s actual final payment date, using whole payout dates.

results.label: Total investment earnings
results.meaning: Total paid minus entered principal. It is distinct from a payout ratio.

compare: Keep principal and effective annual return fixed when comparing payments.
Inspect the last schedule row for a capped final amount.
Compare frequency and horizon separately; this is not a life-contingent quote.
checks: Payments occur at period end.
The annual return is converted to the equivalent monthly, quarterly or annual rate.
No insurance fees, tax or lifetime guarantee is supplied.

pension.answer: Compare plan quotes on the same valuation date with a consistent discount rate, COLA and entered lifespan.

results.label: Present value of pension
results.meaning: Discounted monthly benefit stream through the entered horizon, valued at retirement.

results.label: Pension value advantage
results.meaning: Pension stream value minus entered lump sum; positive does not alone decide suitability.

results.label: Joint-survivor value advantage
results.meaning: Joint and survivor stream value minus single-life stream value for deterministic entered lifespans.

results.label: Undiscounted break-even years
results.meaning: Lump sum divided by initial annual pension; ignores COLA, investment returns and survival probabilities.

compare: Obtain actual benefit and lump-sum quotes from the plan.
Vary lifespan and discount assumptions separately.
Review liquidity, tax and survivor needs outside the numerical comparison.
checks: No salary/service-based pension entitlement calculation.
Benefits occur at monthly end; COLA uses annual anniversaries.
Work Longer excludes salary and additional contributions while working.

social-security.answer: Match the dollar basis of benefit inputs before comparing claiming ages. The highest present value depends on the entered horizon and discount assumptions.

results.label: Highest present-value application age
results.meaning: Best of nine whole ages 62–70 under Ideal mode’s assumptions, not household claiming advice.

results.label: Initial monthly benefit at selected age
results.meaning: Modeled starting benefit before tax and deductions, including assumed waiting COLA in Ideal mode.

results.label: Second option advantage
results.meaning: Compare mode’s second stream PV minus first, both valued at the earlier claim age.

compare: Use SSA estimates and verify whether they include future inflation.
Use Ideal’s common age-62-dollar PIA or Compare’s nominal claim-date quotes consistently.
Vary lifespan and discount rate to understand the sensitivity.
checks: COLA and discount are entered future assumptions, not known future rates.
No earnings-record PIA determination, withholding, benefit tax, Medicare or household survivor coordination.
Actual SSA date, rounding and credit posting rules can differ from the simplified monthly schedule.

fat-fire.answer: This core-plus-lifestyle budget creates a full FIRE target. It is not the discounted Coast threshold, a universal wealth cutoff or a retirement withdrawal guarantee.

results.label: Annual portfolio-funded budget
results.meaning: Monthly costs annualized plus recurring annual provisions and tax allowance, increased by the optional spending buffer.

results.label: FIRE portfolio target
results.meaning: The annual portfolio-funded budget divided by the chosen withdrawal-rate assumption, in today’s USD.

results.label: Age at modeled FIRE target
results.meaning: First whole-month crossing with constant real growth and month-end investments, or an explicit not-reached result at the age limit.

compare: Calculate with a complete budget that counts each expense once.
Review the budget-change table, which changes target size but does not recalculate ages.
Change one budget input and Calculate again to see a different full projection.
checks: All budget entries use today’s purchasing power; do not inflate them again.
Annual provisions are recurring allowances, not dated one-time expenses.
The tax allowance and withdrawal rate are user assumptions; neither is an automatic tax or safety calculation.

lean-fire.answer: This essential-spending budget creates a full FIRE target. It is not the discounted Coast threshold, a universal wealth cutoff or a retirement withdrawal guarantee.

results.label: Annual portfolio-funded budget
results.meaning: Monthly costs annualized plus recurring annual provisions and tax allowance, increased by the optional spending buffer.

results.label: FIRE portfolio target
results.meaning: The annual portfolio-funded budget divided by the chosen withdrawal-rate assumption, in today’s USD.

results.label: Age at modeled FIRE target
results.meaning: First whole-month crossing with constant real growth and month-end investments, or an explicit not-reached result at the age limit.

debt-snowball.answer: This smallest-balance-first projection pays all minimums before directing extra money. The milestones show actual modeled clearance months, not just the initial priority order.

results.label: Months until debt-free
results.meaning: Number of monthly payment periods until every included positive balance is cleared; month 1 is the first payment period, not a calendar date.

results.label: First debt cleared in month
results.meaning: Earliest actual modeled balance clearance. Minimum payments can clear a different debt before the extra-payment target.

results.label: Total interest
results.meaning: Sum of opening balance × APR / 12 each month. Displayed cents are rounded; daily-interest statements may differ.
